newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer, setting contract high.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer, setting contract high.

text.p: Key March three-month Euroyen futures ended firmer on Wednesday, setting a contract high of 99.17 following Japan's industrial output data, traders said.
The March broke through major resistance at 99.14, helped by heavy bids from traders cheered by the data.
The Trade Ministry said June industrial output was down a preliminary 3.1 percent month-on-month, compared with market forecasts ranging from minus 1.2 to minus four percent.
It said it expects manufacturers' output to rise 1.3 percent in July against June but to fall 0.5 percent in August against July.
The next chart resistance for the March lies at 99.20, traders said.
"The underlying tone has been undoubtedly strong as people tend to ignore negative factors and overly react to positive ones," said a European bank trader.
The only threat to the Euroyen market would be the yen's exchange rate. The dollar was drifting well over 118 yen, its strongest since mid-May.
In early trading there was a widespread rumour that Japan's industrial output for June would be down four percent month-on-month, which helped drive up the March contract.

Another rumour, that financier Geroge Soros was beefing up his yen bond portfolio while reducing his Tokyo stock holdings, also added to the bullish sentiment of the yen debt market across the spectrum, traders said.

The Ministry of Finance said will issue a statement on penalties against Nomura Securities and Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd around 5 p.m. (0800 GMT) on Wednesday. The two institutions were involved in payoffs to a racketeer.
Japanese banks paid 5.75 percent to raise three-month dollars in the Euro interbank market on Wednesday, unchanged from Tuesday.

Meanwhile, Yamaichi Securities has generally admitted to allegations of making payoffs to a corporate client widely known to be connected to a "sokaiya" racketeer, a government source close to the investigation said.

A bank trader said: "Yamaichi's scandal will put the broker into an even more difficult financial situation than now, which may persuade the BOJ to hold down rates for a while." -- Yoshiko Mori, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8676
